operations.description:
Submit or update a customer's vote on a specific review.

This endpoint allows an authenticated customer to cast a vote indicating whether they found a review helpful or not. Each customer can vote only once per review, as enforced by a unique constraint on the combination of review_id and customer_id. If a vote exists for this customer-review pair, it will be updated with the new value. Otherwise, a new vote record will be created. The vote type must be either 'helpful' or 'not_helpful'.

The operation is idempotent. The review must exist and be active (not marked as permanently deleted). If the review does not exist or has been permanently deleted, the system returns '404 Not Found'. For any authorization failure (including unauthenticated requests), the system returns '403 Forbidden'.

This operation has no dependencies on other APIs and relies on the review having been previously created through a valid order delivery process.
operations.name: vote

Validate that the requesting customer is authenticated and has the associated review as part of their order history.
Find the review by reviewId and verify it is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL).
Verify the review's shopping_mall_order_item_id links to a completed order item belonging to the authenticated customer.
If an existing vote by this customer for this review exists, overwrite its vote_type field with the new value.
If no vote exists, create a new record in shopping_mall_review_votes with the customer_id, review_id, vote_type, and timestamps.
Use a transaction to ensure atomicity.
Return HTTP 204 No Content on success.
Return 403 if customer is not authorized to vote on this review.
Return 404 if review does not exist or is deleted.

Return 404 if vote not found or if reviewId does not match the vote's review association.

operations.description:

This endpoint provides full audit access to all preserved states of a review, ensuring complete transparency for dispute resolution, compliance, and customer trust. Every edit or deletion of a review creates an immutable snapshot that preserves the review's rating, text, actor, and timestamps exactly as they existed at that moment.

The returned data includes every version of the review from its initial creation through all subsequent edits and final deletions. Each snapshot contains the actor's identity, which allows verification of who made each change. This endpoint is critical for enforcing the platform's snapshot principle that every business-relevant state change must be permanently recorded.

Access to this endpoint is strictly limited to the customer who created the review and platform administrators. Regular users can only view their own review histories. Administrators may access any review's snapshot history for dispute resolution or compliance purposes.

This API operation requires no request parameters beyond the review ID, since all historical data is stored within the shopping_mall_review_snapshots table. The system automatically orders snapshots chronologically by created_at timestamp for consistent viewing.

operations.description:

All changes create an immutable snapshot of the prior version in the review_snapshots table to preserve the historical state for dispute resolution and audit purposes. Review edits are permitted only for reviews with active status, and cannot change the review's association to product, order, or customer. Modifications are not permitted after a review has been deleted. The updated review reflects the changes immediately, but the original review data remains accessible through its snapshot history.

The update is restricted to customers who authored the review. Admins have no direct write access to reviews via this endpoint. All modifications are captured by the snapshot system, ensuring verifiable audit trails for content changes. This operation does not allow changing the review's product, customer, or order association, as these relationships are immutable once established.

After update, the system automatically generates a review snapshot with the prior state. The updated review's updated_at timestamp is refreshed, and the new version is immediately visible to all users. The previous version remains available for audit through the snapshot endpoint. This ensures both current accessibility and historical integrity simultaneously.

Validate that rating is between 1 and 5 if provided. Validate text length is between 0 and 500 characters if provided. Create a review snapshot with the current state of the review before update. Update the review record with new rating and/or text values. Set updated_at timestamp to current time. Return the updated review object with new values. The log entry includes the event type, severity level, timestamp, and optional structured JSON metadata containing diagnostic information such as error stack traces, request IDs, and server identifiers. This endpoint enables administrators to investigate system incidents, verify recovery actions, and generate compliance documentation.

System logs are append-only and cannot be modified, deleted, or overwritten. Access to this endpoint is restricted to administrators due to the sensitive nature of diagnostic information that may contain internal system details.

This operation requires the logId to be a valid UUID. Attempts to request a non-existent log will return a 404 error. The metadata field, if present, will be returned as a JSON string and may contain nested context about the event.

- System logs are generated independently of user actions and cannot be influenced by other endpoints.
- Administrative access to this endpoint is governed by the platform's permission hierarchy.
operations.name: at

Return 500 Internal Server Error if database connection fails. Metadata field is returned as a JSON string and should be serialized as-is without parsing or transforming.

All results return a summary view optimized for performance and display. operations.description:
Retrieve the complete audit record of a specific administrative action performed on the shoppingMall platform.

This endpoint provides detailed visibility into all platform governance actions, including administrator approvals, rejections, suspensions, and other overrides. Each entry in the audit trail captures the full context of the action: which administrator performed it, what entity was affected (seller, product, order, customer, or category), the specific reason for the action, and the exact timestamp of when it occurred.

Access to this information is critical for compliance, dispute resolution, and platform integrity. Administrators can use this endpoint to review historical decisions, verify that proper procedures were followed, and understand the context behind any platform action that affected users or data. The immutable nature of these records ensures that every administrative intervention is permanently traceable for legal and regulatory purposes. This data is stored in the shopping_mall_admin_actions table, which maintains an unchangeable audit log where all records are permanently preserved and cannot be altered or deleted under any circumstances, in accordance with the platform's snapshot principle.

All audit records are generated by the system and reflect actions performed by administrators as defined in the shopping_mall_admin_actions schema. No data in this table is ever modified or removed after creation.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete, immutable historical snapshot of any system entity (product, variant, seller profile, review, etc.) as it existed at a specific point in time.

This endpoint provides forensic-level audit trail access for dispute resolution, compliance reporting, and platform integrity verification. Every change to the system — whether product edits, seller profile updates, review modifications, or cancellation/refund requests — creates a permanently preserved snapshot that captures the entity's complete state before and after the modification.

When you request a snapshot by its unique ID, you receive the unaltered, raw JSON representation of the entity's state exactly as it was captured at the time of the event. This includes all field values, relationships, and metadata. For edits, the snapshot_data contains both "before" and "after" states. For deletions, it captures the final state before removal. This provides an irrefutable record of what was visible to users, what prices were listed, and what seller profiles looked like when transactions occurred.

This access is critical for:
- Resolving customer disputes about product specifications or pricing
- Verifying seller identity during order fulfillment
- Auditing administrative actions
- Meeting regulatory compliance requirements (GDPR, PCI-DSS)
- Recovering data from accidental modifications

All snapshot data is stored in write-once immutable storage and cannot be modified or deleted, even by administrators. This ensures the integrity of the platform's historical record.

This operation retrieves the full snapshot object directly from the shopping_mall_snapshots table. No other API endpoint provides access to this level of historical detail. Any modification attempts to the snapshot data will be blocked by the system.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_snapshots table by snapshotId. Return the entire snapshot_data JSON object exactly as stored in the database. No filtering, transformation, or aggregation. Return 404 if snapshotId does not exist. Ensure read-only access with no side effects. The snapshot_data field contains a fully serializable JSON object representing the exact state of the entity at time of capture, including all fields and relationships.

responseBody.description: The complete, unmodified snapshot data as stored in the database. Contains a serialized JSON object representing the exact state of the entity (product, variant, seller, review, etc.) at the time the snapshot was created. For edits, includes both "before" and "after" states. For deletions, includes the state before removal.

operations.description:
Check the status of email verification for a user account.

This endpoint validates an email verification token provided via the URL path and determines whether it corresponds to an active verification record for either a customer or seller account. The system maintains separate verification records for customers and sellers, each with their own immutable audit trail.

When a user registers, a unique verification token is generated and sent to their email address. The verification record is retained indefinitely in an immutable state for compliance purposes, even after successful verification.

This service is critical for account security and compliance, ensuring that only verified users can access their accounts and preventing fraudulent registrations. Verification records are immutable and permanently preserved in the database, providing an audit trail for security and legal requirements.

operations.description:
Initiate a password reset request for either customer or seller accounts.

This operation allows an authenticated or unauthenticated user to initiate a password reset process by providing their registered email address. Upon receipt, the system generates a temporary reset token with a 1-hour expiration and stores it in the corresponding password reset table (shopping_mall_customer_password_resets or shopping_mall_seller_password_resets). The system does not return the reset token to the client for security reasons. Instead, a confirmation token ID is returned for audit purposes.

The operation is accessible to both customer and seller actors. Upon successful request, the user will receive a password reset email containing a time-limited link. The token viability is strictly enforced at 60 minutes — no extensions or renewals are permitted. Multiple requests can be initiated with the same email, but the system automatically invalidates prior tokens upon new request creation.

This endpoint is intentionally designed without user ID routing to prevent account enumeration. Attackers cannot determine valid user accounts by testing ID paths because email is the sole identifier. This conforms to OWASP security recommendations and the platform's commitment to privacy-first design.

This operation has no effect on the user’s current session. They remain logged in unless explicitly logged out. Only when the reset link is activated does a new session token get issued. No cookies or authentication headers are accepted in this request, as it is designed to function even when the user lacks active credentials.

This endpoint MUST NOT be confused with account creation, login, or authentication. It is purely a password recovery mechanism. It is not intended for verification or account recovery beyond password reset.

Failure conditions:
- If the email is not registered: returns 200 OK for security reason (prevents enumeration)
- If email format is invalid: returns 400 Bad Request
- If rate limiting is exceeded: returns 429 Too Many Requests
- Internal failure: returns 500 Internal Server Error
operations.name: request
operations.specification:
Generate a verifiable unique token ID (UUID) and use it as the primary key for the password reset record.

Look up the account (customer or seller) by provided email in respective tables (shopping_mall_customers or shopping_mall_sellers).

If no account found: create a dummy reset record with a valid token ID, but do not send email — still return 200 OK as defensive security practice.

If account found:
- Invalidate any existing reset tokens for this email in the respective password reset table
- Insert a new reset token record with: token_id, email, user_id (customer_id or seller_id), issued_at (now), expires_at (now + 60 minutes), used: false
- Send password reset email via configured SMTP system with link: https://shoppingmall.com/reset?token={token_id}

Return response with token_id to enable audit trail and user-facing confirmation.

All token generation and email sending must be done in a single transaction with retry logic for email delivery on failure.

Store request method, IP address, user agent (if available), and timestamp in system_logs for behavioral analysis.

Do NOT return the raw token string in the response. Only return the token_id. This prevents token leakage.

Use JSON schema for input validation before processing: email must be valid RFC 5322 email format.

Use indexing and locking on password reset tables to prevent race conditions during concurrent requests.

Restrict POST rate limit to 5 requests per email per hour across all clients. Perform this check before ever querying the database.

Use quarantine buckets for suspicious requests (e.g., repeated invalid emails or malformed payloads).

operations.description:
Reset a user's password using a valid reset token issued during password recovery.

This endpoint allows a user to change their password after successfully validating a password reset token received via email. The operation requires the user to provide the reset token and a new password. The system validates the token against the corresponding password reset record (shopping_mall_admin_password_resets, shopping_mall_customer_password_resets, or shopping_mall_seller_password_resets) to ensure it is active, unexpired, and unmodified. Once validated, the user's password_hash is updated with the new bcrypt-hashed password, the associated reset record is marked as used or deleted, and the user's session is invalidated to ensure security.

This is not a generic update endpoint—it is strictly for password recovery and must only be accessible after a token has been issued. No new password can be set without a valid, unexpired, unvalidated token. The operation follows the transactional pattern where password update and reset token invalidation occur atomically. Authorization is handled by existing JWT session tokens, which must be present in the Authorization header during this request.

Field validation rules:
- password must be minimum 8 characters, containing letters and numbers
- length under 128 characters
- token must match exactly with an active reset record
- the token must not have been used before
- user must be authenticated (Bearer JWT token)

This endpoint does not allow password reset for deleted accounts.

Related operations: GET /password-reset (request token), POST /login (authenticate after reset)

operations.description:
Retrieve the active authentication sessions for the currently authenticated actor (customer, seller, or admin).

This endpoint provides a comprehensive view of the user's active login sessions across their respective actor type. The system resolves the actor type automatically from the session token (JWT) and queries only the appropriate session table (shopping_mall_admin_sessions, shopping_mall_customer_sessions, or shopping_mall_seller_sessions). This ensures strict actor isolation and security compliance by preventing cross-type session enumeration.

Each returned session represents a single authentication event, capturing connection context including IP address, referrer, and timestamps. Sessions are immutable audit records - they are created upon login and become invalid upon expiration, logout, or account suspension. Deleting or modifying sessions is not permitted; they are preserved permanently for security auditing.

The response includes session properties common across actor types: creation timestamp, expiration timestamp, IP address, referrer, and the absolute URL (href) of the page where login occurred. The response structure preserves actor context to prevent ambiguity: the actor type is embedded in the response schema through the leading prefix "shopping_mall_" in the table name context.

This endpoint is not used for troubleshooting sessions or initiating logout - to terminate a session, use platform logout functionality, which revokes the refresh token and invalidates the session at the protocol level.

operations.description:
Terminate an active session by invalidating its JWT tokens and marking it as inactive.

This endpoint implements session termination for both admin and customer authentication sessions. According to the system's audit trails design, all session records are immutable and append-only. This operation does not delete the session record but instead sets the is_active flag to false to indicate that the session has been terminated.

This pattern ensures that all authentication events are permanently preserved for security auditing, compliance, and forensic analysis. The actual JWT tokens (access_token and refresh_token) are not stored for future validation but are immediately invalidated with this operation.

The system maintains separate session tables for admin and customer actors, but both follow the same audit pattern: session ID is a UUID, a created_at timestamp is recorded, and the session is terminated by setting is_active to false when logout occurs or tokens expire. This endpoint allows users to manually terminate their sessions before automatic expiration.

The session identified by sessionId must exist in either the shopping_mall_admin_sessions or shopping_mall_customer_sessions tables, as these are the only session entities maintained by the system. Attempting to terminate a non-existent session will return a 404 error.

Note: This operation leaves the session record intact for historical audit purposes. The session is logically deleted (soft delete) by the is_active flag and cannot be restored.

operations.description:
Terminate an active session by invalidating its JWT tokens and marking it as inactive.

This endpoint implements session termination for both admin and customer authentication sessions. According to the system's audit trails design, all session records are immutable and append-only. This operation does not delete the session record but instead sets the is_active flag to false to indicate that the session has been terminated.

This pattern ensures that all authentication events are permanently preserved for security auditing, compliance, and forensic analysis. The actual JWT tokens (access_token and refresh_token) are not stored for future validation but are immediately invalidated with this operation.

The system maintains separate session tables for admin and customer actors, but both follow the same audit pattern: session ID is a UUID, a created_at timestamp is recorded, and the session is terminated by setting is_active to false when logout occurs or tokens expire. This endpoint allows users to manually terminate their sessions before automatic expiration.

The session identified by sessionId must exist in either the shopping_mall_admin_sessions or shopping_mall_customer_sessions tables, as these are the only session entities maintained by the system. Attempting to terminate a non-existent session will return a 404 error.

Note: This operation leaves the session record intact for historical audit purposes. The session is logically deleted (soft delete) by the is_active flag and cannot be restored.

operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive administrative dashboard with aggregated platform metrics.

This endpoint provides administrators with a real-time overview of the shoppingMall platform's operational status, enabling effective oversight and informed decision-making. The dashboard displays essential statistics across all core domains of the platform, including seller activity, order volume, product distribution, and system health metrics.

The data presented is derived from immutable snapshot records and represents the authoritative state of the platform. The statistics reflect the entire platform ecosystem and are computed from the complete history of transactions, approvals, suspensions, and system events. This ensures administrators can make decisions based on verified, unchangeable historical data rather than volatile or manipulable real-time data. The dashboard does not allow modifications - all administrative actions must be performed through dedicated endpoints (e.g., force-cancel, force-refund, approve-seller).

System administrators use this dashboard as their primary interface for platform management, monitoring for anomalies, identifying trends, and ensuring platform integrity. The aggregated metrics enable rapid identification of systemic issues such as sudden drops in seller approvals, spikes in cancellation requests, or abnormal inventory adjustments.

The dashboard includes data from all administrator actions recorded in the shopping_mall_admin_actions table, seller statuses from the shopping_malls_sellers table, order statuses from the shopping_mall_orders table, product listings from the shopping_mall_products table, and system-level events from the shopping_mall_system_logs table. All data is presented in summary form to avoid overwhelming administrators with raw data while still providing comprehensive insights.

The response includes a timestamp of when the summary data was last computed, ensuring administrators know the recency of the information they are reviewing. This timestamp is based on the system's processing time, not the current wall-clock time, maintaining consistency with the platform's immutable data model.

Query admin_actions, sellers, orders, products, and system_logs tables to compute aggregated metrics.
- Count total administrators (active and inactive)
- Count total sellers by status: approved, rejected, suspended, pending
- Count total orders by status: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, partially completed
- Count total products with active variants
- Count total pending cancellation requests
- Count total pending refund requests
- Count total system logs from the last 24 hours
- Compute total transaction volume (sum of all order totals)
- Compute average order value
- Compute seller approval rate (approved / total applications)
- Compute customer retention rate based on repeat order data
- Compute inventory turnover rate
- Return all metrics in a single summary object with timestamp of computation.
- All data must be derived from immutable snapshots, not live tables.
- Return only the summary object with no pagination, as this is a single summary endpoint.

This endpoint provides a high-level overview of all orders placed by the authenticated customer, showing the current status of each order as derived from its constituent order items. The status reflects the aggregate state of all items within an order, which can be 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', 'refunded', or 'partially completed'.

This API is designed for customer order history views where users need to quickly assess the status of their orders without loading detailed item information. The response includes only essential summary data to optimize performance for listing views.

For detailed information about specific orders, including items, shipping, and pricing, customers should use the GET /orders/{orderId} endpoint.

The status value is calculated server-side by aggregating the statuses of all order items according to the business rules defined in the shopping_mall_orders model, ensuring consistency across all client applications. All data reflects the state at the time of the request.

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated revenue statistics for the shoppingMall platform.

This endpoint provides comprehensive revenue reporting for administrators, calculating total commission income from all completed transactions. Revenue is derived from the 7.5% commission rate applied to each order's total value, as defined in the business model. All financial calculations are based on immutable order item snapshots stored in the database, ensuring that revenue figures reflect the exact pricing, discounts, and product states at time of purchase, not current values.

The system maintains immutable financial records so that administrators can generate accurate reports that cannot be manipulated by changes to product prices, seller profiles, or discount policies after the fact. Each order item's unit_price and quantity are captured from the cart snapshot at checkout, forming a legally defensible audit trail for financial reporting.

This endpoint supports administrative functions including financial auditing, investor reporting, tax compliance, and platform profitability analysis. All revenue data is tied to the same immutable snapshot architecture that preserves product, variant, and seller states at time of transaction.

Related operations:
- The data returned by this endpoint is based on the order_items table, which is populated through the checkout process described in 07-order-management.md
- The commission calculation (7.5%) is defined in 03-business-model.md and applied as a system rule
- No direct interaction with inventory or cart data occurs - revenue is derived solely from completed order items with status 'delivered'
- The results must be accurate regardless of subsequent changes to products or sellers, relying entirely on snapshot data

Error handling:
- If no orders exist within the requested period, returns an empty data array with pagination
- Invalid date formats return 400 Bad Request with specific field errors
- Non-admin actors receive 403 Forbidden response
- Database connection issues return 500 Internal Server Error with appropriate logs.

Business context:
- All financial calculations are based on the exact state preserved in order_item snapshots
- The system does not adjust revenue figures retroactively if a seller's commission rate changes
- Revenue tracking is independent of seller suspension or account deletion - historical revenue remains intact
- No direct API interaction with user accounts or product listings affects this data

Security requirements:
- Only admin actors can access this endpoint
- All results are read-only - immutable snapshot data cannot be modified
- All access attempts are logged in shopping_mall_admin_actions
- Response data should never be cached for more than 1 hour to prevent stale reporting

Data integrity:
- Revenue calculation: sum(order_item.quantity * order_item.unit_price * commission_rate)
- Commission rate is fixed at 0.075 (7.5%) as defined in shopping_mall_system_settings
- All calculations are performed using precise decimal arithmetic to avoid rounding errors
- Results must match the exact amounts recorded in the system's financial audit trails

Return results with pagination using cursor-based strategy to handle large datasets efficiently. Use SQL window functions to calculate totals for each page without full table scans. operations.description:
Update a shipment record's status in a controlled manner according to platform business rules.

This endpoint allows only specific status transitions for shipment records as defined by the shoppingMall platform's immutable audit principle. When a customer receives their order, they may confirm delivery, which triggers a status change from 'shipped' to 'delivered'. The system will also automatically change the status to 'auto-delivered' after 14 days if delivery has not been confirmed by the customer. This endpoint is designed to maintain a verifiable, unchangeable audit trail for all delivery events.

No other status transitions are permitted. Attempting to set the status to 'shipped' on an already shipped record (or any other unauthorized state change) will result in an error. The system strictly enforces that shipment status can only progress forward and cannot be reverted or set to arbitrary values. The carrier and tracking number information may be updated once to ensure accuracy of delivery tracking, but any subsequent changes to tracking details must create a new shipment record rather than modifying the existing one.

This operation works in conjunction with the order item status transitions. When a shipment's status changes to 'delivered' or 'auto-delivered', the system automatically updates the associated order items' status to 'delivered' as well. This ensures full consistency between the physical delivery record and the digital order status.

The endpoint is protected to prevent unauthorized access - only customers who placed the order or system-level processes can initiate status updates. This design reinforces the platform's foundational principle that all commercial transactions must leave an immutable, verifiable audit trail that cannot be manipulated retroactively.

Check current shipment status - only allow status update from 'shipped' to 'delivered' or 'auto-delivered'. Validate that status parameter is one of the allowed values: 'delivered' or 'auto-delivered'. If status is 'delivered', record confirmation metadata including timestamp, IP address, and device information. If status is 'auto-delivered', verify that 14 days have passed since shipment creation. Update the shipment record with new status and any provided tracking information. Ensure the carrier name and tracking number are provided and valid (alphanumeric, 8-32 characters). Validate that the tracking number is unique and properly formatted. Update the associated order items' status to match the new shipment status. Log all status transitions in the immutable audit trail. Return the updated shipment record with current status and timestamps.

operations.description:
Confirm delivery of a shipment to complete the order fulfillment cycle.

This endpoint allows a customer to formally confirm receipt of their ordered items. Once confirmed, the shipment status transitions from "shipped" to "delivered", which triggers several downstream business processes including enabling product review submission, initiating the 7-day refund eligibility window, and potentially activating loyalty or rewards programs.

This confirmation is critical for maintaining data integrity in the platform's immutable audit trail. The system does not permit multiple delivery confirmations for the same shipment, and once confirmed, the delivery status becomes permanently locked. The customer can confirm delivery via a mobile app, web interface, or automated system notification.

For security and privacy, this operation verifies that the authenticated customer owns the specific shipment being confirmed. The system matches the customer's authenticated account with the order item associated to the shipment, preventing unauthorized delivery confirmations. The confirmation event itself is permanently recorded with customer device signature, IP address, and exact timestamp for dispute resolution and legal compliance.

This operation is directly related to the POST /shipments endpoint, where sellers create shipment records, and the PATCH /shipments/{shipmentId}/tracking endpoint, where tracking information is updated. This confirmation operation represents the final step in the fulfillment workflow.

When a customer does not confirm delivery within 14 days, the system automatically performs this confirmation on their behalf, as defined in the automatic delivery policy. This customer-initiated confirmation takes precedence over any automatic confirmation. Once a manual confirmation occurs, automatic delivery will be canceled for that shipment.

This enables customers to track the status of their refund requests and understand expected resolution timelines.

For audit and dispute resolution, this endpoint provides complete historical visibility into all refund activity. The refund requests are tied to specific order items, preserving the exact product, variant, price, and seller information as it existed at time of purchase. All refund request records are permanently preserved in the system with no deletion capability.

This operation is read-only and does not alter any data. The permanent record ensures compliance with financial and consumer protection regulations requiring immutable audit trails.

Security: Only the seller who owns the products associated with these requests can access this information. The endpoint automatically filters requests based on the authentication context, ensuring sellers can only see requests for their own products.

Business context: This endpoint is critical for seller dispute resolution workflows. Sellers have a time-limited window (48 hours for cancellations, 72 hours for refunds) to respond to these requests before automatic approval occurs. This dashboard provides the primary interface through which sellers manage these time-sensitive business decisions.

Related operations:

- GET /seller/requests/history - View historical responses to completed requests

Retrieve immutable audit trail records from the shopping_mall_snapshots table.

This endpoint provides a comprehensive historical audit trail of all significant changes made to platform entities including products, variants, seller profiles, reviews, and administrative actions. Every change to the system is permanently recorded as an immutable snapshot to ensure integrity for compliance and dispute resolution.

The audit trail captures exact state changes for: entity modifications, seller actions, customer reviews, and administrator interventions. Each record contains the full before-and-after state of the entity at the moment of change, along with the actor responsible and precise timestamp.

This functionality is critical for regulatory compliance (GDPR, CCPA, PCI-DSS), forensic investigations, and resolving business disputes where historical accuracy is paramount. Administrators can reconstruct exactly how a product appeared, what a seller's profile looked like, or how a review was modified at any point in time.

The endpoint supports filtering by entity type (product, variant, seller_profile, review, cancellation_request, refund_request), actor ID, time range, and action type (created, edited, deleted, approved, rejected, canceled, refunded). Results are sorted in descending chronological order and use cursor-based pagination to handle potentially large audit volumes efficiently.

This endpoint is read-only and no modifications to the audit records are permitted under any circumstances.

Use query parameters exclusively - no path parameters allowed.

Administrators use this dashboard to proactively detect system anomalies, investigate incidents, and validate operational stability. The data is not for transactional purposes but for forensic analysis and preventative maintenance.

This endpoint leverages the platform's unique snapshot architecture, where every administrative action is permanently recorded with full context. The data shown represents unalterable records, providing the highest assurance for legal and compliance purposes.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete immutable history of a seller's profile changes.

This endpoint returns a chronological list of all snapshot records of a seller's shop name, description, and logo as they appeared at the time of each change. This history is critical for platform administrators to audit changes and for dispute resolution. Each snapshot captures the exact state of the seller's profile at the moment it was edited, ensuring that historical representations of the seller are permanently preserved.

According to the platform's mandatory snapshot principle (12-snapshot-principle.md), all profile modifications are recorded as immutable snapshots in the shopping_mall_seller_profile_snapshots table. These records are never deleted, modified, or overwritten.

This operation is accessible only to administrators, as indicated by the /admin/ path segment. The returned snapshots are ordered from most recent (newest) to oldest. Each snapshot contains only the data as it existed at that point in time — not the current state. Even if a seller updates their name or logo today, all previous snapshots remain unchanged and accurately reflect how the seller appeared during past transactions.

This endpoint does not return the current profile (which is not stored in shopping_mall_seller_profiles due to violation of the snapshot principle) — only historical snapshots.

Do not join with other tables; snapshots are self-contained.
Return list of up to 50 snapshots (primarily, very few projects have >10).

Seller information includes the shop name, description, and logo exactly as shown on the marketplace at the time of transaction to preserve reputation context.

This structure ensures absolute data integrity: even if the product is renamed, the variant is modified, or the seller changes their profile, the customer's order history always reflects the precise state of the marketplace at the moment of purchase. No live data is ever displayed. All information is derived from immutable snapshots stored in the system.
